observations: Single used automotive mount component photographed on a concrete/stone surface.
Photo 0 and 1 show the metal bracket with two integrated rubber-cushioned posts and a small circular emblem visible on the black rubber/plastic center, consistent with a Mercedes-Benz tri-star logo.
Photo 2 shows the same part held in a hand, giving a sense of scale (fits in one palm), with the Mercedes logo also faintly visible in the center.
No part number, stamped code, or box/label is visible in any photo.
Surface shows oxidation/dirt consistent with a used (tokunbo) part; no cracks or tears in the rubber bushing are clearly visible, but image resolution and angle limit inspection.
No underside, mounting bolts, or engine-bay installation photo is provided.

claims.claim: High grade tokunbo (used import, high quality)
claims.evidence: Condition grading like 'high grade' cannot be confirmed from static photos; no stress test or close-up of rubber integrity shown.
No part number or chassis-specific marking visible in any photo to confirm exact fitment range.
Logo is visible in photo 0/1/2 but could be an aftermarket replica stamped with the emblem; no OEM part number visible to cross-check.

risks.risk: Rubber bushing may be cracked, torn, or perished internally, reducing lifespan despite external appearance.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rubber cushion from multiple angles, plus a flex/press test video.

risks.risk: Exact model/part number mismatch causing fitment failure on buyer's specific chassis variant.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any embossed part number or OEM sticker on the metal bracket underside.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unconfirmed-fitment mount, not model-specific guaranteed part

risks.risk: Hidden corrosion or metal fatigue on the mounting ears/bolts not visible from current angles.
risks.proof: Photo of underside and bolt holes close up, plus photo of the mount removed showing full profile.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having unverified structural integrity, worst case treated as needing replacement bolts/ears

risks.risk: Mount could be mislabelled as 'gear mount' when it may actually be an engine mount, changing its application and value.
risks.proof: Photo showing where the part was removed from in the vehicle (engine bay vs transmission tunnel), or a labeled diagram match.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic used engine/transmission mount without confirmed exact application

proof_requests: Close-up of any embossed part number or OEM sticker on the metal casting.
Photo of the underside and all four mounting ears/bolt holes.
Video showing a press/flex test on the rubber bushing to demonstrate no internal cracking.
Photo showing the exact location in the donor vehicle where this mount was removed (engine or transmission side).
response.reason: The item is clearly a used Mercedes-Benz engine/transmission mount identifiable by the visible logo, but with no part number or fitment proof, it must be priced as a generic unverified-fitment used mount with unconfirmed rubber condition.
